description: A picturesque village and transit hub situated amidst the rolling pine-forested hills of Ri-Bhoi district along the scenic Guwahati-Shillong expressway (NH 6).
why_visit: Take a scenic mountain break on the winding highway to Shillong, breathe fresh pine-scented mountain air, and savor steaming Khasi-style momos and fresh local pineapples.
hidden_gem_reason: A charming hillside respite along the expressway, surrounded by unspoiled Khasi pine hills.
activities: Highway Sightseeing; Local Pineapple & Fruit Tasting; Mountain Photography
distance_from_nearest_famous_place: 25 km from Nongpoh along GS Road (NH 6)
notes: Famous for roadside stalls selling organic Kew pineapples and ginger.

description: Plunging dramatically from a 1,115-foot (340 m) high cliff in the wettest plateau region on Earth into an ethereal turquoise-green plunge pool, recognized as India's tallest unsegmented plunge waterfall.
why_visit: Witness the raw power of India's tallest plunge waterfall surrounded by mist-covered Khasi canyons, photograph the vibrant turquoise plunge pool, and explore nearby living root bridges.
best_time_to_visit: October to April for clear turquoise pool; July to September for roaring monsoon cascade
activities: Waterfall Viewpoint Photography; Canyon Trekking; Local Khasi Honey Buying; Living Root Bridge Exploration
distance_from_nearest_famous_place: 5 km from Sohra market / 54 km from Shillong
notes: Name means 'Jump of Ka Likai' based on tragic Khasi folklore; viewpoints have binoculars and local souvenir stalls.

place_name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge (Jingkieng Nongriat)
subcategory: Centuries-Old Indigenous Bio-Engineering Marvel Grown from Ficus Elastica
description: An astonishing 250-year-old two-tiered botanical bridge grown by indigenous Khasi villagers across the Umshiang River by intertwining the living aerial roots of Ficus elastica trees over generations.
why_visit: Hike down 3,500 stone mountain stairs through lush tropical rainforests to witness humanity's most extraordinary living bio-architecture, and swim in natural crystal-blue plunge pools under the bridge.
hidden_gem_reason: Hidden deep inside a dense Khasi river canyon requiring an exhilarating 3,500-step trek, preserving an authentic and pristine tribal ecosystem.
best_time_to_visit: October to April for clear trekking paths and turquoise river pools
activities: 3,500-Step Rainforest Trekking; Living Root Bridge Photography; Natural Plunge Pool Swimming; Rainbow Falls Hike
distance_from_nearest_famous_place: 12 km from Cherrapunji (trailhead at Tyrna village)
notes: Homestays available in Nongriat village for overnight recovery; carry trekking poles for 3,500 stairs.

subcategory: Acclaimed Cleanest Village in Asia & Bamboo Skywalk
description: Awarded the title of 'Cleanest Village in Asia' in 2003 by Discover India, an immaculate floral hamlet where 100% literacy, community waste composting in conical bamboo bins (Khoon), blooming orchid gardens, and treehouse skywalks overlook Bangladesh plains.
why_visit: Stroll down spotless cobblestone pathways flanked by vibrant flowerbeds, climb the 85-foot bamboo Skywalk for panoramic views of Bangladesh floodplains, and walk to the nearby Riwai single-decker living root bridge.
hidden_gem_reason: A pristine model community village championing 100% eco-tourism, indigenous waste management, and traditional Khasi matrilineal hospitality.
best_time_to_visit: October to April (Post-monsoon freshness & pleasant weather)
activities: Village Walking Tour; Bamboo Skywalk Climb; Riwai Living Root Bridge Trek; Khasi Homestay Experience; Traditional Matrilineal Culture Study
distance_from_nearest_famous_place: 75 km south of Shillong / 18 km from Dawki
notes: Smoking and single-use plastics are strictly prohibited throughout the village.

subcategory: World-Famous Glass-Clear River & Riverside Pebble Camping
description: Flowing between India and Bangladesh through green Jaintia gorges, the Umngot River is internationally celebrated for crystal-clear emerald water so transparent that wooden country boats appear to float on thin air above the riverbed pebbles.
why_visit: Ride wooden rowboats that look suspended in mid-air over underwater pebbles and fish, camp under starry skies on the pebble beaches of Shnongpdeng, and enjoy cliff jumping and scuba diving.
best_time_to_visit: November to February (Water reaches maximum transparency and clarity)
activities: Glass-Clear River Boating; Riverside Pebble Beach Camping; Kayaking; Snorkelling; Cliff Jumping; Suspension Bridge Walk
distance_from_nearest_famous_place: 82 km south of Shillong / Indo-Bangladesh Border
notes: Transparency decreases significantly during monsoon rains; winter offers peak glass-like clarity.

subcategory: Spectacular Turquoise Natural Plunge Pool & Walkway Behind Cascade
description: Hidden within dense subtropical forests of the Jaintia Hills, a magical waterfall dropping over a broad limestone ledge into an otherworldly crystal turquoise-blue natural pool, equipped with stone-paved walkways and a cavernous path directly behind the falling curtain of water.
why_visit: Swim safely in the turquoise-blue natural pool wearing provided life jackets, walk along stone pathways directly behind the roaring water curtain, and take in the emerald jungle amphitheatre.
hidden_gem_reason: A breathtaking natural turquoise pool and curtain waterfall tucked inside the Jaintia Hills, far less commercialized than Cherrapunji falls.
best_time_to_visit: September to April (Turquoise pool color is most vibrant outside monsoon flood peaks)
activities: Natural Pool Swimming with Life Jackets; Walking Behind Water Curtain; Cliffside Photography; Forest Trail Hiking; Riverside Camping
distance_from_nearest_famous_place: 30 km from Jowai / 90 km from Shillong
notes: Wearing a lifejacket is strictly mandatory for entering the water; lifeguards on duty.
